topic: Phase 2 expansion commissioned March 2026 (capacity to 22.5 mtpa)
wiki_text: On 31 March 2026, Petronet LNG commissioned the Phase 2 expansion of the Dahej LNG terminal, raising the facility's nominal regasification capacity by 5 MMTPA from 17.5 to 22.5 MMTPA, making it India's largest LNG import terminal. The expansion, underway since around 2022, provides additional regasification slots and more flexible import scheduling.

topic: Environmental clearance for expansion to 26.2 mtpa (Sept 2025)
wiki_text: On 2 September 2025, the Expert Appraisal Committee of India's Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change granted environmental clearance for Shell Energy India's expansion of the Hazira LNG terminal from 6.28 to 26.2 MMTPA, an investment of about Rs 21,600 crore. The expansion includes new LNG storage tanks, a jetty for conventional LNG carriers, a breakwater, and 2.8 million cubic metres of capital dredging. An earlier 10 MMTPA expansion plan had stalled in 2021 over pending forest clearance. No final investment decision has been announced.

topic: Breakwater completed; terminal becomes all-weather (June 2025) and planned expansion
wiki_text: In June 2025, GAIL completed the Dabhol breakwater, making the terminal an all-weather port able to receive LNG cargoes year-round including the southwest monsoon; the first monsoon-season cargo was discharged from the vessel GAIL Bhuwan on 2 June 2025. As of May 2025 GAIL planned to expand Dabhol's regasification capacity to 6.3 MMTPA by mid-2027 and to 12.5 MMTPA by 2031-2032 (an additional 7.5 MMTPA over the current 5 MMTPA).

topic: Construction progress (92.3% as of Dec 2025) and AG&P FSRU/FSU joint venture
wiki_text: As of 31 December 2025, the Swan LNG (Jafrabad) FSRU project in Amreli district, Gujarat, had reached 92.3% physical progress with a stated completion deadline of September 2026, per the Gujarat Legislative Assembly. In December 2024, Swan Energy and AG&P Terminals and Logistics signed a heads of agreement to form a JV to provide the FSRU and a floating storage unit (FSU) to operationalise the terminal, with AG&P holding 51% and Swan Energy 49% of the vessel-provision venture. The terminal's nameplate capacity is 5 MMTPA, expandable to 10 MMTPA.

topic: Hoegh Giant FSRU charter terminated; AG&P acquisition talks
wiki_text: Hoegh LNG terminated the charter of the 170,000-cbm FSRU Hoegh Giant with India's H-Energy (effective April), citing the charterer's default of contractual terms; H-Energy disputed Hoegh's entitlement to terminate but accepted that the FSRU contract is at an end, leaving the Jaigarh terminal without a committed FSRU. Separately, Singapore-based AG&P (Nebula Energy) has been in negotiations to acquire H-Energy's Jaigarh LNG terminal; as of latest reporting the acquisition had not closed.
